name: Taj Mahal
description: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the banks of the Yamuna River. Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal.
history: Constructed over 22 years (1632-1653) by approximately 20,000 workers. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1972.
photography: Excellent - especially at sunrise and sunset

name: Agra Fort
description: Red sandstone fortress built by Emperor Akbar. One of the most impressive monuments in India.
history: Built in 1565, the fort served as the residence of emperors for over 200 years. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Jaipur City (Pink City)
description: The pink-colored old city of Jaipur, planned on the Vastu Shastra and Shilpa Shastra principles. A marvel of urban planning.
history: Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II. UNESCO World Heritage Site (2019).

name: Amber Fort
description: A magnificent 5-story fortified palace set into a hillside. One of Rajasthan's most iconic fortresses.
history: Built in 1592 by Raja Man Singh, the fort showcases a blend of Hindu and Mughal architecture.
accessibility: Cable car available, limited wheelchair access

name: Khajuraho Temples
description: A group of 22 Hindu and Jain temples with intricate stone carvings. Famous for their erotic sculptures.
history: Built between 10th-12th centuries during the Chandela dynasty. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A 13th-century temple dedicated to Surya (Sun God), designed in the shape of a chariot with 12 wheels.
history: Built around 1250 CE by Narasimhadeva I. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

name: Ellora Caves
description: A site of 34 Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain caves carved into a volcanic basalt cliff face. Spans 5 centuries of rock-cut architecture.
history: Excavated between 5th-10th centuries CE. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.

name: Ajanta Caves
description: 29 Buddhist rock-cut caves with ancient paintings and sculptures dating back to the 2nd century BCE to 5th century CE.
history: Carved into horseshoe-shaped gorge. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983. Contains earliest Indian paintings.

name: Humayun's Tomb
description: The first garden-tomb in India, built by Humayun's first wife and chief consort Bega Begum. A precursor to Taj Mahal.
history: Commissioned in 1565-1572 CE, 9 years after Humayun's death. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993.
highlights: Red sandstone and white marble work

name: Red Fort
description: A 17th-century Mughal fortress that served as the residence of the emperors. A symbol of Indian independence.
history: Built by Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638-1648. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007. Independence flag hoisted here annually.

name: Mahabalipuram Temples
description: 7th-century Pallava dynasty temples with monolithic rock structures and intricate carvings. Situated on the Coromandel Coast.
history: Built during 7th-8th centuries. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984. Ancient port city history.

name: Hampi Ruins
description: Ruins of Vijayanagara Empire capital with extensive temples and monuments scattered across a stunning landscape.
history: Capital of Vijayanagara Empire (1336-1565 CE). UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986. Abandoned after 1565 war.

name: Varanasi Ghats
description: Sacred ghats (steps) along the Ganges River in the oldest inhabited city of India. Center of Hindu spirituality and culture.
history: Oldest inhabited city - mentioned in ancient texts. Over 80 ghats with rituals dating back millennia.
photography: Excellent - be respectful at cremation ghats

name: Mathura
description: Birthplace of Lord Krishna - one of the holiest sites in Hinduism. Home to numerous temples and spiritual significance.
history: Ancient pilgrimage city mentioned in Puranas and Hindu scriptures. Important center since antiquity.

name: Vrindavan
description: Holy city of Krishna's childhood. Known as the 'Land of Eternal Love'. Center of Radha-Krishna worship.
history: Ancient pilgrimage site associated with Krishna's pastimes. Over 5,000 temples in the city.
accessibility: Wheelchair accessible in main temple areas

name: Rishikesh
description: Yoga capital of the world. Sacred Hindu pilgrimage city on the banks of Ganges with ashrams and spiritual institutions.
history: Ancient pilgrimage site mentioned in Hindu texts. Became yoga center due to presence of many ashrams.

name: Haridwar
description: Gateway to the gods - one of the holiest Hindu pilgrimage cities. Site of Kumbh Mela (every 12 years).
history: Ancient pilgrimage city mentioned in Puranas. Gateway where Ganges emerges from mountains.

name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
description: The most sacred shrine of Sikhism. Famous for its stunning gold-plated dome and spiritual atmosphere.
history: Completed in 1604. Sanctified by Sri Adi Granth (Sikh holy scripture). Largest free kitchen (langar) in the world.

name: Tirupati Temple
description: The most visited Hindu temple in the world. Dedicated to Lord Venkateswara. Major pilgrimage site with rich history.
history: Built in 11th century. One of the 108 Divya Desams (sacred shrines of Hinduism).

name: Meenakshi Temple
description: Ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi. One of the most important Hindu temples with stunning architecture.
history: Legend dates to 3600 BCE. Current structure from 6th-17th centuries. One of the largest temples in India.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
description: One of the most sacred Hindu temples. Dedicated to Lord Shiva. Located in the heart of Varanasi on Ganges banks.
history: One of the 12 Jyotirlingas (sacred shrines of Shiva). Golden spire donated by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

name: Shirdi (Sai Baba Temple)
description: Sacred shrine dedicated to Saint Sai Baba. Spiritual healing center attracting millions of pilgrims annually.
history: Sai Baba lived here (1838-1918). Samadhi Mandir (mausoleum) built at his sacred site.

name: Kedarnath Temple
description: One of the 12 sacred Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. Located in the highest Himalayas. Major pilgrimage destination.
history: Ancient temple (mentioned in Vedas). High altitude location in Chopta Range. Part of Char Dham pilgrimage.

name: Rameshwaram
description: One of the four holiest pilgrimage sites in Hinduism. Located on Pamban Island. Temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
history: Ancient pilgrimage city - where Lord Rama worshipped Shiva. Part of Char Dham pilgrimage.

name: Udaipur City Palace
description: The largest palace complex in Rajasthan. Stunning Indo-Aryan and Mughal architecture overlooking Lake Pichola.
history: Built in 1559. Still partially royal residence. Beautifully blends traditional and modern architecture.

name: Jaisalmer Fort
description: Golden sandstone fort in the Thar Desert. 12th-century Rajput fortress with 99 bastions and temples inside.
history: Built in 1156 CE by Jaisal Singh. UNESCO World Heritage Site (tentative list). Desert gateway.

name: Mehrangarh Fort
description: 15th-century fortress towering over Jodhpur. Part of the 'Blue City'. Offers panoramic views of the region.
history: Built by Rao Jodha in 1459. One of India's most impressive forts. Museum with royal artifacts.

name: Gwalior Fort
description: 8th-century fortress with strategic importance. Features Man Singh Palace and Jai Vilas Palace museum.
history: One of India's most impressive forts. Witnessed many dynasties. Important during Mughal and British periods.

name: Chittorgarh Fort
description: Largest fort in Rajasthan. 7 gates and 5 towers. Associated with legends of honor and bravery.
history: Built in 7th century. Associated with Rani Padmavati and stories of women's courage. Symbol of Rajput valor.

name: Jodhpur (Blue City)
description: The Blue City - distinctive blue-painted old city. Characterized by Mehrangarh Fort backdrop and Marwari culture.
history: Founded in 1459. Blue color tradition since 19th century. Important trading hub historically.

name: Mysore Palace
description: Indo-Saracenic architectural marvel. Royal residence of the Wodeyar dynasty. One of India's finest palaces.
history: Built in 1897. Combines Hindu, Islamic, and Gothic architectural styles. Current palace built after 1897 fire.

name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
description: Iconic 5-story pink sandstone structure with 953 small windows. Unique architectural design of Jaipur.
history: Built in 1799. Designed by Lal Chand Ustad. Allows cool breeze through windows - innovative design.

name: Ranthambore Fort
description: 10th-century fortress surrounded by Ranthambore National Park. Ancient temples and wildlife sanctuary combined.
history: Built in 10th century. Significant during Mughal and British periods. Now surrounded by Tiger Reserve.

name: Darjeeling
description: Queen of Hill Stations. Famous for tea plantations, Kanchenjunga views, and toy train rides.
history: British hill station established in 19th century. World-famous Darjeeling tea. UNESCO Toy Train heritage.
photography: Excellent - mountain views and tea gardens

name: Shimla
description: Former summer capital of British India. Famous for Mall Road shopping, Ridge views, and toy train.
history: Established as hill station in 1819. Served as summer capital of British India. UNESCO toy train heritage.

name: Mussoorie
description: Adventure capital of India. Famous for Gun Hill views, Kempty Falls, and adventure sports.
history: Established in 1823 by British officer F.S. Canning. Popular hill station with adventure activities.

name: Ooty (Ootacamund)
description: Queen of South Indian Hill Stations. Famous for tea gardens, Nilgiri Mountain Railway, and botanical gardens.
history: British hill station established in 1821. Home to world-famous tea plantations and toy train.

name: Munnar
description: Highest peak in Kerala. Tea and spice plantations in green Ghats. Tea trekking and plantation tours available.
history: Developed by British as tea plantation area. Important tea-producing region. Popular trekking destination.

name: Nainital
description: Lake surrounded by mountains. Popular hill station with boating, trekking, and adventure sports.
history: Established in 1841 by British. Naini Lake forms the heart of the town. Important pilgrimage site.

name: Manali
description: Adventure sports capital of India. Famous for Rohtang Pass, Solang Valley skiing, and trekking.
history: Named after Manu (Hindu legend). Important trading hub in ancient times. Modern adventure destination.

name: Goa Beaches
description: Beach paradise of India. Famous for beaches, Portuguese architecture, watersports, and vibrant nightlife.
history: Portuguese colony until 1961. Unique culture mixing Indian and Portuguese influences.

name: Kerala Backwaters
description: Network of lagoons and lakes. Houseboat cruises through palm-fringed backwaters offer serene experience.
history: Ancient trading route. Influenced by Arab, Chinese, Jewish, and European traders historically.

name: Andaman & Nicobar Islands
description: Tropical island paradise with crystal clear waters, coral reefs, and virgin beaches.
history: Colonial history - Cellular Jail. Now important tourism destination with unique biodiversity.

name: Ranthambore National Park
description: Tiger reserve with dense forests and scenic landscape. Popular for tiger sightings and wildlife photography.
history: Established in 1980. One of India's premier tiger reserves with good tiger population.
